summary: No orders today: bitcoin bounced to about $64,000, but that is still well below all of its averages, it has spent only part of one UTC day back above $62,000, and I found no sign yet of money returning to the US bitcoin funds, so none of my conditions for buying back has been met.
thesis:
Where the account stands. The account is $988.30 in cash and holds no coins, about 1.2% below its $1,000 start. A plain $1,000 bitcoin holding bought on 11 November was worth $827.34 at the end of 22 November, so the account is about $161 ahead of simply holding bitcoin. All of that lead comes from having been out of the market since 14 November, and the lead has narrowed by about $32 over the last two days as bitcoin recovered.

What happened. Bitcoin's last price of 22 November on Coinbase was $61,163, up 1.8% on the day. On Monday 23 November it traded around $61,000 to $61,700 through the early hours UTC, then climbed with a rebound in US technology shares, reaching about $63,900 at 14:33 UTC and holding above $64,000 in later reports. Ether rose to about $1,825, solana to about $77 and XRP to about $1.01 in the same mid-afternoon reading, each up 7% to 11% on the day. The reports I read found no single cause beyond the stock market bounce and sellers who had bet on further falls being forced to buy back. The widely followed fear and greed gauge was still 11 out of 100, "extreme fear". The US bitcoin funds have lost about $3.5 billion in November so far, and I found no report of money coming back in on Friday 20 November or Monday 23 November. A senior Federal Reserve official has said a half-point rate rise may be needed in December, and US inflation figures due on 25 November could move all risky markets.

The trend. Using the figures collected for this account (last price of 22 November), and with bitcoin now near $64,000, it is about 8% below its 20-day average ($69,330), about 17% below its 50-day average ($76,660) and about 11% below its 200-day average ($72,320). It has fallen 20% over 20 days and 28% over 60. Every other watched coin is also below all three of its averages and down 20% to 26% over 20 days. Under the plan this is still the lowest band, near the bottom of it while bitcoin is clearly below its 200-day average.

The case for buying, taken seriously. Bitcoin is now about 15% above Saturday's low, has climbed back over the $62,000 level it fell through, and fear readings this extreme have sometimes come close to the bottom of a fall. If today ends above $62,000, that is the first of the two UTC days my small-first-step condition asks for. But the condition also needs the bitcoin funds to report money coming in on at least two trading days, and so far they have not reported any. A one-day jump driven by a stock bounce and forced buying back, with the Fed leaning toward higher rates, is exactly the kind of move that has reversed several times this month. Waiting one or two more days for the conditions costs a few percent at most if the turn is real; buying early costs more if it is not.

What would bring me back, unchanged. I will buy bitcoin again if it ends a UTC day back above its 200-day average, now about $72,300, or earlier with a smaller amount (about 15% to 20% of the account) if it holds above $70,000 for two UTC days while the bitcoin funds take in money on most days. I will take a small first step, about 10% of the account, if bitcoin ends two UTC days above $62,000 and the funds report money coming in on at least two trading days. This view is wrong if Saturday's low proves to be the bottom and bitcoin keeps climbing, in which case the account buys back higher and gives back more of its lead.
risks: The main risk is missing a rebound that is already well under way: bitcoin is about 15% above Saturday's low and ether and solana are rising faster, so a recovery could go further before my conditions are met and the account's lead over bitcoin would keep shrinking. Prices here come from news reports taken at different times; the latest firm reading is from mid-afternoon UTC, and bitcoin can move several percent before midnight UTC. I found no fund-flow figures for 20 or 23 November, so the flow condition may already be closer to being met than I can see.
